summary_en: Inventor collaborations across European regions are usually one-shot — only a small fraction of co-inventor pairs collaborate again. Elekes asks what makes a collaboration repeat. Using EPO patent data on co-inventors across NUTS-3 regions, he finds that geographic proximity, prior personal ties, and similarity in technological profile all raise repeat-collaboration probability, but the effects are concentrated in regions outside the European core. Peripheral regions rely on stickier inventor relationships to access knowledge from the core.
data_used: European Patent Office (EPO) patent data, geocoded to NUTS-3 regions, restricted to co-inventor pairs spanning multiple regions. Repeat-collaboration is identified within multi-year windows; estimation uses logit models with region-pair fixed effects.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian and EU regional R&D policy (NKFIH, Horizon Europe, EFRE smart-specialisation): the paper shows that for peripheral regions like most of Hungary outside Budapest, durable inventor relationships are more important for absorbing core-region knowledge than fresh introductions. Programme design should therefore prioritise repeat-collaboration funding instruments over one-off matchmaking — relevant for ITM's industry–academia linkage scheme and EFRE-funded R&D vouchers.
title: Repeated collaboration of inventors across European regions
